input_text: No one nice to animals is also mean to animals. Some grumpy people are mean to animals. All animal lovers are nice to animals. All pet owners love animals. Tom is a pet owner. If Tom is not both a grumpy person and mean to animals, then Tom is neither a grumpy person nor an animal lover?
answer:
Let me work through this.

Tom is a pet owner → Tom loves animals → Tom is nice to animals → Tom is not mean to animals.

Now check the condition: "If Tom is not both a grumpy person and mean to animals" — Tom is not mean to animals, so Tom is not both a grumpy person AND mean to animals. The condition is satisfied.

Therefore: Tom is neither a grumpy person nor an animal lover.

But Tom loves animals (established above), so Tom IS an animal lover — contradiction with the conclusion that Tom is not an animal lover.

The question asks whether the conclusion (Tom is neither a grumpy person nor an animal lover) is true.

The statements establish Tom IS an animal lover, so the conclusion that Tom is not an animal lover is false.

False
